We need to produce a tok model for the described process. Let's parse description.

Title: Inspection of an Energy Drink Bottling Machine

Process: The organization invests in inspection app.

Actors? The text mentions "you" as user perhaps. So one pool organization, lane for user (maybe "Inspector" or "Operator").

Steps:

- Start
- Enter type of machine, and its serial number => a task: "enter machine type and serial number".
- Inspection can begin => maybe start of inspection sub flow.

Then activities: "Questions are asked, and you have to input values." => task "answer inspection questions". Could be multiple questions, but we can model as a task.

- "Buttons are to be pressed, and values are automatically collected from the machine and shown to you." => task "press buttons and collect values".

These two can happen maybe in parallel? The description: "* Questions are asked, and you have to input values. * Buttons are to be pressed, and values are automatically collected from the machine and shown to you." They seem sequential maybe both part of inspection step. Could be parallel? The instruction: use parallel gateways for activities that happen at same time. Are they simultaneous? Possibly they can be done in any order but not necessarily parallel. Might treat as parallel: The inspector can answer questions while also pressing buttons? Could be separate tasks but could be done sequentially. To be safe, we might model a parallel split: after entering machine data, split into two parallel tasks: "answer inspection questions" and "press buttons and collect values". Then join.

- "Depending on the results, additional questions are asked (or not)." So after the parallel join, we have a decision: if results require additional questions -> task "answer additional questions". else skip. Then end.

Thus flow: start -> task "enter machine type and serial number" -> parallel gateway split (and) -> task "answer inspection questions" and task "press buttons and collect values" -> parallel gateway join (and) -> exclusive gateway "additional questions needed?" with two branches: yes -> task "answer additional questions" -> end; no -> directly end.

We need to define pool and lane.

Pool ID maybe "org". Lane ID "inspector". Use `pool org "Inspection Organization" { lane inspector "Inspector" }` ?

In tok, syntax: `pool org "Inspection Organization" { lane inspector "Inspector" }`. Then tasks inside lane identified with lane prefix? I think tasks can be placed inside lane with `task ID "Label"` preceded by lane? Actually in tok, you define `lane` then within block you define elements. Example from cheat sheet: `pool p "Company" { lane sales "Sales" { start s "Start"; task t "Do work"; end e "End" } }` Not sure exact syntax; but typical.

We need to write a tok file with header `tok 1.0`. Also we might need `executable`? Not required, just model. So use `tok 1.0`.

Add flows.

Identifiers: start s; end e; tasks: enter-info, answer-questions, press-buttons, answer-additional.

Gateway IDs: split and join (and). Decision xor with id "needs-more".

We'll need to reference lane tasks: they are inside lane block; flow definitions use IDs.

Let's draft:

```
tok 1.0

pool org "Inspection Organization" {
  lane inspector "Inspector" {
    start start "Start"
    task enter-info "Enter machine type and serial number"
    and split "Parallel activities"
    task answer-questions "Answer inspection questions"
    task press-buttons "Press buttons and collect values"
    and join "Join parallel activities"
    xor needs-more "Additional questions needed?"
    task answer-additional "Answer additional questions"
    end end "End"
  }
}

flow start -> enter-info
flow enter-info -> split
flow split -> answer-questions
flow split -> press-buttons
flow answer-questions -> join
flow press-buttons -> join
flow join -> needs-more
flow needs-more -> answer-additional when="result = \"yes\""
flow needs-more -> end when="result = \"no\""
flow answer-additional -> end
```

Need to mark default? there are two outgoing flows from xor; each need when attribute or default. We'll use when conditions or default on one. Use when for yes, default for no.

Better:

```
flow needs-more -> answer-additional when="additional = true"
flow needs-more -> end default
```

Thus we meet exclusive gateway rule.

Also we need to ensure that after answer-additional we go to end.

All good.

Now check with tool.

# tok 1.0 — cheat sheet

One statement per line. Blocks by indentation (spaces). `#` starts a comment.
Every statement starts with a keyword. Identifiers: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`, unique. Labels: "quoted text".
Attributes: `key=value` (value: word, number or "text") and bare flags. A key or flag is written once per line, the triggers of
multiple events aside (in 1.0 a repeated one is the deprecation warning `R090`).

```
tok 1.0 "Title" [executable]                       # header, first line (0.1–0.7 documents stay valid)
    [process-name="Name"] (process of a document without pools)   doc="Text" on any statement: documentation

start ID "Label" [message="M" | timer=P3D | signal="S" | condition="feel"] [form=F]
end ID "Label" [message="M" | error="E" | escalation="X" | signal="S" | terminate]   # error/escalation: [code="E1"]
catch ID "Label" message="M" | timer=PT2H | signal="S" | condition="feel" | link="L"
throw ID "Label" [message="M" | escalation="X" | signal="S" | link="L" | compensate]
boundary ID "Label" on=ACTIVITY timer=P7D [noninterrupting]   # also message/error/escalation/signal
    several triggers = multiple event: message="A" message="B" signal="C"; + parallel = all of them (catching)
    trigger not given yet: flags message timer signal condition error escalation (start ID "Label" message)

task | user | manual | service | script | rule | send | receive | call   ID "Label"
    flags: loop parallel sequential compensation
    user … form=F        rule … decision=D result=var        script … expr="feel" result=var
    service … type="job"  send/receive … message="M"          call … process=P | task=GLOBAL
    loop while="feel" [test-before] [loop-max=5]              receive … instantiate (starts the process)
    service|send|receive … operation=OP                       user … by=RESOURCE (performer)
sub ID "Label"           # embedded sub-process: indented block with its own start and end

eventsub ID "Label"      # event sub-process: block starts with a start event with a trigger

tok 0.3 "T" executable version-tag="v1"   pool p … version-tag="v1"
```

Language 0.5 elements (transaction, cancel, complex, loop conditions, multiple events, instantiate, process data,
global tasks, operations, keys) and 0.6 elements (conversations, choreographies, min/max) are BPMN only:
`--level basic|analytic` rejects them, and in executable documents for Camunda they are reported as `C100`–`C123`.
Decisions of 0.7 are level `full`; Camunda codes `C130` (bkm with invoke=), `C131` (non-literal function body),
`C132` (decision without logic).
In 0.5 documents `resource` and `by=` also export BPMN performers.

Commands: `tok check F [--class descriptive|analytic|common-executable|full]` · `tok fmt F [-w]` · `tok bpmn F` ·
`tok svg F` · `tok export F [-o DIR]` (0.7: NAME.dmn + NAME.drd.svg per decision graph) · `tok import F.bpmn|F.dmn [-o F.tok]`
(BPMN: writes F.tok.layout, the drawing reused by bpmn/svg/export; `--no-sidecar`) · `tok sim F` ·
`tok eval F DECISION name=value …` (0.7: with required decisions; JSON values `x='{"a": 1}'`) · `--lang pl` · `--json`
